title: Debug Traceboard — consolidated failed request explorer
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a single, discoverable 'Debug Traceboard' in Redwood Console that surfaces failed requests, retries, error taxonomy, and request payload inspection in a lightweight, developer-friendly UI. This board should help engineers and SREs quickly triage production failures, understand retry behavior, and map errors to rollout/config changes or model variants. The goal is to reduce mean-time-to-diagnosis for transient and systemic errors while keeping data-access controls and PII redaction in mind.
acceptance_criteria: A browseable Traceboard view accessible from Console -> Observability -> Errors
Ability to filter and group failed requests by time range, route, model, region, and release tag
Compact timeline view that shows initial failure and subsequent retries with expandable lanes
Payload inspector that shows request inputs and model responses with redaction toggle and 'safe sample' masking
Error taxonomy badges (e.g., network, model-runtime, decoding, rate-limit, auth) with count breakdowns
Quick actions: open incident ticket template, link to related logs, deep-link to Dedicated pool or Private deployment
Keyboard navigation for list and timeline expansions
Design handoff artifacts (Figma + specs) and a prioritized engineering tickets list
decisions: Surface Traceboard as a top-level page under Observability rather than a modal to allow persistent filters and deep-linking
Use a two-column layout: left for list & taxonomy filters, right for timeline + payload inspector, to keep inspection context visible
Represent retries as connected timeline nodes to make retry cascades visually traceable
Implement a read-only 'replay preview' for requests (no execution) that shows tokenized diffs and model variant used
Default payload view will redact detected PII; user can toggle 'show masked' if they have console data access
Prioritize performance: timeline should stream sample rows and lazy-load payloads to avoid blocking the console
tradeoffs: Full request replay vs read-only preview: we chose preview to avoid accidental re-execution and security surface area
Side panel inspector vs persistent right column: persistent column increases surface area but keeps context when navigating failures
Detailed per-token diffs add developer value but increase render complexity; implemented as collapsed sections behind a toggle
review_feedback: PM (Rajiv): prefer a pill for release tags to correlate incidents to rollouts — add affordance to correlate by rollout ID
Eng (Maya): backend needs compact API that returns minimal payloads and a separate endpoint to fetch full request body; ensure lazy loading behavior
Security (Omar): require explicit consent + audit log for unredacting PII; surface role-based control in the inspector
Design (Nina): confirm color usage for error taxonomy meets contrast and is accessible to color-blind users
SRE (Tom): include a 'retry chain heatmap' export for offline analysis and incident reports
open_questions: What degree of sampling is acceptable for high-volume routes before we start aggregating failures?
How will Dedicated / Private environments expose request payloads — will there be additional redaction rules?
Should the Traceboard be writable for on-console annotations (comments) vs linking to external incident systems?
next_steps: Incorporate feedback and update hi-fi prototype (due 2025-02-24)
Coordinate with backend to define two endpoints: trace-summary and trace-detail (specs by 2025-02-28)
Run 3 unmoderated usability sessions with platform engineers and SREs (goal: 6 participants)
Create engineering tickets for: filters, timeline rendering, payload inspector, RBAC redaction toggles
notes: This design intentionally scopes out active request replay in the first iteration to reduce risk.
We will track Mean Time To Diagnose (MTTD) and time-to-ticket-creation as primary KPIs for the next quarter.
Prototype includes keyboard shortcuts: 'j/k' to move rows, 'enter' to expand, 'r' to open retry heatmap
